originalAction.text: Metformin’s established glucose-lowering action combines reduced glucose production by the liver, reduced intestinal glucose absorption and improved uptake and use of glucose by tissues. It improves insulin sensitivity without stimulating insulin secretion. Repurposing research asks whether changes in cellular energy sensing, growth signals and the handling of damaged cellular material can be useful beyond diabetes. AMPK is an energy-sensing enzyme, while mTOR signaling helps regulate protein production and cell growth; altering these systems can have different consequences in infected cells, tumors and healthy muscle. The evidence below distinguishes effects measured in experimental models from proposed explanations and from clinical outcomes, because demonstrating a pathway change does not establish that a treatment helps patients.

AMPK is an energy-sensing enzyme, while mTOR signaling helps regulate protein production and cell growth; altering these systems can have different consequences in infected cells, tumors and healthy muscle.

The evidence below distinguishes effects measured in experimental models from proposed explanations and from clinical outcomes, because demonstrating a pathway change does not establish that a treatment helps patients.

pathways.title: Insulin sensitivity and growth signaling
pathways.text: Improving insulin sensitivity is part of metformin’s established action in diabetes. In cancer repurposing, reducing insulin-related growth stimulation is one proposed route to benefit. The MA.32 breast-cancer trial measured changes in insulin, weight and other metabolic factors, but its clinical report did not show improved invasive disease-free survival. These findings distinguish a measured metabolic effect from an unconfirmed anticancer benefit.

pathways.title: AMPK, mTOR and the balance between energy use and growth
pathways.text: AMPK activation and reduced mTOR signaling provide a rationale for changing cell growth and protein production. In myeloma cell lines and mouse xenografts, metformin activated AMPK, suppressed mTORC1 and mTORC2 signaling, and was associated with autophagy, cell-cycle arrest and reduced tumor growth. In viral infection, suppression of host-cell protein production is a proposed explanation for reduced SARS-CoV-2 replication; the COVID-OUT nasal-swab study measured viral RNA rather than directly proving that mTOR mediated the reduction in viral RNA. The same growth-related pathways also matter in healthy tissue: mTORC1 supports muscle growth, and metformin reduced muscle gains during resistance training in the MASTERS trial. A mechanism that appears useful in one setting can therefore work against the intended outcome in another.

pathways.title: Autophagy and mitochondrial stress
pathways.text: Autophagy is the cell’s process for recycling cellular material. In Parkinson’s disease cell and mouse models, metformin was associated with AMPK activation and autophagy, less mitochondrial oxidative stress and reduced accumulation of alpha-synuclein. Blocking AMPK or autophagy weakened protection in toxin-injured cells, supporting a contribution from these pathways within that model. Inhibitor specificity, the experimental exposure and the difference between toxin injury and human disease limit translation; these experiments do not establish that metformin slows Parkinson’s disease in people.

pathways.title: Complex I inhibition and energy sensing
pathways.text: Two preclinical studies in cells and isolated mitochondria show that metformin inhibits complex I of the mitochondrial respiratory chain, the enzyme that initiates electron transfer during cellular respiration. In intact hepatoma cells, 50 micromolar metformin produced time-dependent inhibition of complex I activity, reducing glutamate oxidation by 13 percent after 24 hours and 30 percent after 60 hours; succinate oxidation, which enters at complex II, was unaffected, confirming selectivity for complex I. In a complementary study using isolated rat hepatocytes, inhibition of cell respiration by metformin occurred only in intact cells and not in permeabilized cells or isolated mitochondria, demonstrating that the mechanism requires an indirect, cell-mediated signaling step rather than direct drug contact with the enzyme. In isolated sub-mitochondrial particles, half-maximal inhibition required approximately 79 mM, far above therapeutic plasma concentrations, while the effect appeared at 50 micromolar in intact cells, consistent with intracellular drug accumulation. Reduced flux through complex I lowers cellular ATP production and is proposed to be one upstream trigger for the AMPK activation described in other pathway studies. These are preclinical findings from cell lines, isolated hepatocytes, and sub-cellular fractions; they do not establish the concentrations, tissue distribution, or extent of complex I inhibition during therapeutic metformin treatment in people.

guides.description: How metformin works, its investigated benefits across infections, cancer, neurological conditions and physical function, and its safety.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: What is metformin?
sections.paragraph: Metformin is an oral glucose-lowering medicine in the biguanide class. In the United States, immediate-release metformin tablets are approved alongside diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes in adults and children aged 10 years and older. It reduces the liver’s glucose production and improves the body’s response to insulin; those established uses are distinct from the repurposing investigations discussed here. Researchers are studying whether its effects on metabolism, cellular energy sensing and inflammatory pathways can help in acute COVID-19 and Long COVID, Parkinson’s disease, cognition in schizophrenia, and age-related loss of muscle function. Cancer research includes trials in prostate, lung, breast and pancreatic cancer, studies of recurrent colorectal adenomas after polyp removal, and laboratory work in multiple myeloma. The findings vary by condition and outcome: promising biological effects have often failed to translate into clinical benefit, and preventing a condition, treating established disease and changing a laboratory marker are different questions.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: The benefits being investigated include reducing Long COVID risk, improving cognition in schizophrenia, preserving physical function in older adults and improving Parkinson’s symptoms. A small schizophrenia trial reported improved cognitive-test scores with metformin, while the Parkinson’s pilot and the MET-PREVENT sarcopenia trial did not demonstrate improvements in their main clinical outcomes. For Long COVID, COVID-OUT reported a prevention signal, although a correction notice and inconsistent control percentages complicate interpretation; ACTIV-6 did not meet its primary efficacy threshold, and a separate trial found no improved recovery after symptoms were established. Cancer trials have generally not demonstrated the hoped-for treatment benefits; a separate colorectal study found fewer recurrent adenomas after polyp removal, which is a prevention outcome.

questions.question: Does metformin improve symptoms of Parkinson’s disease?
questions.answer: A three-month pilot randomized 60 people to metformin or placebo alongside levodopa/carbidopa. Clinical scores improved within the metformin group, but the comparison between groups did not show a statistically significant benefit on the total Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale. The trial was small, used a per-protocol analysis and was too short to establish whether metformin slows disease progression.

questions.question: What has the schizophrenia research found about cognition?
questions.answer: In a 72-person open-label randomized trial, adding metformin to antipsychotic treatment improved the composite cognitive-test score by an estimated 3.43 points more than antipsychotics alone after 24 weeks (95% CI 1.83–5.02). The participants were predominantly young adults, 59 completed follow-up, and the study lacked a placebo group; larger blinded studies are needed to confirm the size and practical importance of this effect. A later analysis of the same trial linked changes in metabolites and hippocampal connectivity with cognitive changes.

questions.question: Does metformin improve muscle strength or physical function?
questions.answer: The 2025 MET-PREVENT trial randomized 72 older adults with probable sarcopenia and prefrailty or frailty to metformin or placebo for four months. It found no walking-speed benefit: the adjusted difference was 0.001 m/s (95% CI −0.06 to 0.06), and metformin was poorly tolerated in this population. The 2023 review described inconsistent results: some research suggested faster walking, but strength outcomes were not consistently improved and exercise adaptations could be reduced. In the MASTERS trial, adding metformin to resistance training reduced muscle growth in healthy older adults; the difference in strength gains was not statistically significant.

questions.question: Does taking metformin during COVID-19 prevent Long COVID?
questions.answer: COVID-OUT reported fewer later clinician-diagnosed cases when treatment began during acute infection, but the estimate remains provisional because the report contains inconsistent control percentages and has a published correction. ACTIV-6 examined symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months and did not meet its prespecified threshold for benefit. The trials enrolled different populations and used different outcomes, leaving uncertainty about how much prevention benefit metformin provides.

questions.question: Does metformin help when Long COVID is already established?
questions.answer: A randomized South Korean trial did not find improved recovery after a two-week course of metformin in people with persistent symptoms. That result concerns the population and short treatment course tested; it does not establish the effect of longer courses or treatment in every Long COVID subgroup. A separate metformin-and-fluvoxamine fatigue report was retracted and republished; its original findings cannot serve as reliable evidence of metformin benefit.

questions.answer: STAMPEDE randomized 1,874 men with metastatic hormone-sensitive disease. Overall survival did not improve significantly: hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.80–1.03. Adverse metabolic effects of androgen deprivation were reduced.

questions.question: Is the colorectal finding about cancer treatment or prevention?
questions.answer: It concerns prevention of recurrent adenomas and polyps after removal. In the one-year trial, adenoma recurrence was lower with 250 mg daily metformin, with a reported risk ratio of 0.60, 95% CI 0.39–0.92. Survival after established cancer was not the endpoint.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Metformin commonly causes diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal discomfort; longer use can lower vitamin B12. Its major serious risk is lactic acidosis, particularly with impaired kidney function, hypoxia, liver disease or excessive alcohol intake.

questions.question: What monitoring is relevant?
questions.answer: Kidney function and vitamin B12 are relevant monitoring targets; certain contrast scans, surgery or acute hypoxic illness can require temporary interruption.

sentences.text: Kidney function and vitamin B12 are relevant monitoring targets; certain contrast scans, surgery or acute hypoxic illness can require temporary interruption.

questions.question: What did the Long COVID prevention trial report about safety?
questions.answer: ACTIV-6 found no safety concern for its selected low-risk adult population, but monitored lactic acidosis and medically diagnosed hypoglycaemia rather than comprehensively measuring tolerability.

sections.label: Contraindications
sections.paragraph: Contraindications include eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m², metabolic acidosis and metformin hypersensitivity; starting treatment at eGFR 30–45 is not recommended.

sections.label: Interactions
sections.paragraph: Insulin or sulfonylureas increase hypoglycaemia risk; topiramate can increase acidosis risk; cimetidine, dolutegravir and ranolazine can increase metformin exposure. Excessive alcohol also increases lactic-acidosis risk.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.title: What schedules have repurposing trials tested?
sections.paragraph: The COVID-OUT and ACTIV-6 prevention trials tested a 14-day course of immediate-release metformin, increasing to 1,500 mg daily. The Parkinson’s pilot used 500 mg twice daily for three months, while the schizophrenia trial used up to 1,500 mg daily for 24 weeks. These studies tested different treatment schedules for different conditions; they did not establish one repurposing dose or demonstrate equivalent outcomes with extended-release metformin.

These studies tested different treatment schedules for different conditions; they did not establish one repurposing dose or demonstrate equivalent outcomes with extended-release metformin.

questions.question: What are the labeled starting dose and titration schedule for immediate-release metformin?
questions.answer: The U.S. prescribing information for immediate-release metformin tablets lists a starting dose of 500 mg twice daily or 850 mg once daily, taken with meals. The dose is increased by 500 mg each week or by 850 mg every two weeks, based on glycemic control and tolerability, up to a maximum of 2,550 mg per day in divided doses. The label notes that doses above 2,000 mg per day may be better tolerated when divided into three doses taken with meals. These are the labeled regimens for type 2 diabetes; repurposing trials used their own schedules.

questions.question: What is the labeled starting dose and maximum for extended-release metformin?
questions.answer: The U.S. prescribing information for extended-release metformin tablets recommends starting at 500 mg once daily with the evening meal. The dose is increased by 500 mg each week based on glycemic control and tolerability, up to a maximum of 2,000 mg once daily with the evening meal. The label states that patients already receiving immediate-release metformin may switch to the same total daily dose as extended-release taken once daily. The extended-release label does not include a pediatric dosing section.

questions.question: Do immediate-release and extended-release metformin have the same efficacy and tolerability?
questions.answer: A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis of nine randomized controlled trials in 2,609 adults with type 2 diabetes found that extended-release metformin produced statistically worse but likely clinically similar HbA1c lowering compared with immediate-release. Extended-release reduced dyspepsia relative to immediate-release but did not significantly reduce overall gastrointestinal intolerance, including diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, and nausea. The U.S. prescribing information for each formulation describes its own dosing regimen and does not assert equivalent glycemic efficacy across formulations.

questions.question: How should metformin dosing be adjusted based on kidney function?
questions.answer: Both the immediate-release and extended-release U.S. prescribing information require assessment of kidney function (eGFR) before starting metformin and periodically during treatment. Starting metformin is not recommended when eGFR is 30 to 45 mL/min/1.73 m2; metformin is contraindicated and should be discontinued when eGFR falls below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. A 2014 systematic review in JAMA of metformin in type 2 diabetes and kidney disease found that lactate concentrations are not substantially increased at eGFR values of 30 to 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and concluded that cautious use with dose monitoring is warranted in mild-to-moderate chronic kidney disease.

questions.question: What does the U.S. label say about metformin dosing in children?
questions.answer: The U.S. prescribing information for immediate-release metformin tablets includes an indication for type 2 diabetes in children aged 10 years and older. The labeled starting dose for this age group is 500 mg twice daily with meals, increased by 500 mg each week based on glycemic control and tolerability, with a maximum of 2,000 mg per day in divided doses. The extended-release U.S. prescribing information covers adult dosing only and does not include a pediatric dosing section.

sections.label: Results
sections.paragraph: In the schizophrenia trial, the between-group difference in the composite cognitive-test score was 3.43 points at 24 weeks (95% CI 1.83–5.02). MET-PREVENT found a walking-speed difference of 0.001 m/s at four months (95% CI −0.06 to 0.06). The South Korean Long COVID trial reported recovery in 84 of 132 participants receiving metformin (63.6%) and 90 of 132 receiving placebo (68.2%) at eight weeks.

sections.label: Status
sections.paragraph: The U.S. prescribing information lists metformin as an adjunct to diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes in adults and children aged 10 years and older. The cancer, COVID-19, Parkinson’s disease, cognition and sarcopenia investigations discussed here are repurposing research; these are not indications listed in that metformin-tablet prescribing information.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The human evidence spans prevention, treatment and physical or cognitive function, with different populations, comparators and follow-up periods. Several cancer trials did not demonstrate the expected clinical benefit; adenoma recurrence after polyp removal is a separate prevention outcome. The schizophrenia metabolite and imaging report analyzes the same trial as the earlier cognitive report, so it does not add a second independent trial. Cell and mouse findings explain biological rationale but cannot establish patient benefit. COVID-OUT has a published correction notice and conflicting control-group percentages in the available report. Its long-term diagnosis estimate should be read with that qualification. The original REVIVE fatigue report has a notice of retraction and republication; its original results are not used as evidence of benefit.
